backlog.spec: Use a 20% explore phase. During refinement, alternate the hop base between the best and the second-best distinct packing (sum differs by more than 1e-4). Update both when a hop result beats the second best. Return the best.
backlog.title: Explore fraction 20 percent with refinement restarts from a top-2 pool

backlog.spec: In cons, require the pair distance to be at least r_i + r_j + 1e-9. The wall constraints should be c - r >= 1e-9 and the same for the other walls. SLSQP then returns packings that are already valid, and _repair loses almost nothing. Reduce SHRINK to 1e-11 accordingly. Check validity at the end and fall back to the full repair if needed.
backlog.title: Margin-aware constraints

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, build the perturbed start from the best packing as follows. Shrink all radii to 0.7 times their values and add centre noise of sd 0.01. Run SLSQP for 60 iterations and then for the full MAX_ITER iterations from the result. Compared with the 0.9 shrink, the circles have more room to rearrange before they re-expand.
backlog.title: Grow-radius continuation from best

backlog.spec: After _repair produces a valid (c, r), run one pass in a random order (drawn from the seed rng). For each circle i, set r_i to the largest value allowed by the walls and by every other circle j, which is min(c_i to walls, d_ij - r_j for all j). Do not decrease any radius. Accept the inflated radii only if the packing stays valid under the harness tolerance, and compare by r.sum() before storing best. This recovers slack that the shrink-based repair leaves behind, at O(n^2) cost per pass.
backlog.title: Greedy radius inflation after repair

backlog.spec: Add a third perturbation move in _solve_once when start is given: with probability 0.3 (leave relocate and jitter sharing the remaining 0.7 equally), draw a random point p uniform in the unit square and a factor s = rng.uniform(0.90, 0.98), then set c0 = p + s * (c0 - p) for all centres whose distance to p is below 0.4 (others unchanged), and add tiny noise rng.normal(0, 0.003) to those moved centres. This opens slack on one side of a region so SLSQP can rearrange it. Radii start at r0 * 0.9 as now. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Compress-toward-a-point perturbation

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, keep a current packing cur and a best packing best. Perturb cur, not best. Accept the new result if its sum is greater than cur_sum - T*(-log(u)), with T = 0.003 and u uniform in (0,1). Always track the global best separately and return it. This gives a slightly looser acceptance than strict improvement, and it is meant to escape local optima.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, after each SLSQP run, identify rattlers as circles with no contact within 1e-4 of any wall or other circle. Pick one rattler at random, and move its centre to the grid point (on a 60 by 60 grid) with the largest clearance to the other circles and walls. Set its radius to that clearance, then run SLSQP warm-started from this configuration with the reduced maxiter of 100. Keep the result only if sum r improves. This targets slack that removal-and-reinsert moves hit only at random.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation into the largest hole

backlog.spec: In the relocate branch of _solve_once, the 2 to 4 relocated circles are chosen uniformly. Choose them instead with probability proportional to 1 / (r0 + 0.02) ** 2 (normalised to sum to 1, passed as p= to rng.choice with replace=False), so that small, poorly placed circles are moved far more often than the large ones that form the backbone of the packing. Keep the number relocated, their new uniform positions, the 0.5 * INIT_RADIUS starting radius, the jitter branch and the acceptance rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Bias relocation towards small circles

backlog.spec: For 50% of the explore-phase fresh restarts, set the initial radii by size class. The 4 circles nearest the corners get 0.14, 12 get 0.10 and the rest get 0.06. The random centres stay as they are. The other 50% keep the standard INIT_RADIUS. Keep the 30% explore and refinement structure of slot 9.
backlog.title: Size-class start in explore phase for half of restarts

backlog.spec: In the refinement phase, for about 30% of starts, keep the centres of the best packing exactly as they are. Reset every radius to 0.5 times the minimum radius of the best packing, then run SLSQP in full from this start. The centres are unchanged, so the search explores how radii can regrow around the same arrangement, which differs from jittering the centres. Compare results as usual by r.sum() after repair.
backlog.title: Radius-reset warm start from best centres

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, change the jitter branch (the else branch that adds normal noise of sd 0.02 to all centres) so that it perturbs only a local cluster. Pick one circle i at random with rng.integers(n), find its k nearest circles by centre distance with k = rng.integers(3, 7) (the set includes i itself), and add rng.normal(0, 0.05, (k, 2)) to those centres only; all other centres stay exactly as in the best packing. Keep r0 * 0.9 for all radii, keep the relocate branch and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Local-neighbourhood jitter instead of global jitter

backlog.spec: Add an optional maxiter argument to _solve_once (default MAX_ITER) and pass it to the SLSQP options. In solve, call it with maxiter=80 when refining from the best packing (not explore), and keep 200 for fresh random restarts. Since refinement starts near a good local optimum, fewer iterations should suffice and the number of hops in the remaining time roughly doubles. Keep the greedy acceptance, repair and everything else the same.
backlog.title: Shorter SLSQP runs in refinement for more hops

backlog.spec: Make no change to the refinement logic of the incumbent. Only add a constant SEED_OFFSET = 1000 to the seed used in np.random.default_rng(seed + SEED_OFFSET) so the run is an independent replicate. This estimates whether the -2.6360 result was luck, so later tuning has a real baseline.
backlog.title: Replicate slot 9 unchanged with a different seed offset

backlog.spec: Add a cheap local hop used in the refinement phase with probability 0.5 (otherwise use the current perturbation unchanged). Pick a random circle and its m = 8 nearest circles (9 in total, the 'window'). Randomise the window: jitter its centres by normal noise sd 0.04 and set its radii to 0.6 of their values. Then run SLSQP (maxiter 150) over only the 27 window variables, with constraints: window-window non-overlap, window versus each fixed circle non-overlap (fixed centres and radii are constants), wall constraints and r >= 0 for window circles; the objective is minus the sum of the window radii. Write the result back into a copy of the best packing, clip, run _repair on the full packing and accept if the total sum improves. The sub-problem is far smaller, so many more hops fit in the time.
backlog.title: Frozen-window sub-problem hops

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres in _solve_once with a scrambled Halton or Sobol-style sequence in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2. Use a random digit scramble or random offset drawn from the seed rng so each restart differs, and keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Low-discrepancy points cover the square more evenly, so restarts explore a wider set of initial layouts for the same number of SLSQP calls.
backlog.title: Low-discrepancy initial centres

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, in the shake branch (else), apply noise only around one spot instead of to all circles: pick a random centre p = c0[rng.integers(n)], find the circles whose centres lie within 0.3 of p, and add rng.normal(0, 0.03, (m, 2)) to those centres only. All other circles stay exactly as they were. Keep the clip and the r0*0.9 radii as now. A local kick rearranges one region without breaking the rest of the packing.
backlog.title: Local neighbourhood shake

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when a start is given, the initial radii are now r0 * 0.9. Change this to r0 * 0.97 so warm starts begin closer to the incumbent and SLSQP needs fewer iterations to get back to a tight packing. Keep the fresh-start radius INIT_RADIUS and all other logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Milder radius shrink on warm starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, in the relocate branch, place each moved circle in a hole instead of at a random point. Sample 2000 candidate points uniformly in [0.02, 0.98]^2 with rng. For each candidate, compute its clearance: the minimum over the non-moved circles of (distance - radius), and also the distance to the nearest wall. Assign the moved circles one by one to the candidates with the largest clearance, and after each assignment treat the placed circle (radius = clearance*0.9) as an obstacle. Set its initial radius to 0.9 * clearance, with a minimum of 0.005. All other code stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Hole-targeted relocation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add a third warm-start move. With the start given, draw u = rng.random(): if u < 0.4 do the existing relocate move; if u < 0.8 do the existing centre shake; otherwise keep the centres but multiply the radii by np.exp(rng.normal(0, 0.25, n)) and then scale all radii by 0.85. This changes which circles are big or small and lets SLSQP find a different size arrangement on almost the same geometry. Use rng for all randomness.
backlog.title: Radius-noise move

memo:
Helped: only slot 9 (30% random restarts, then perturbing the best packing with an acceptance rule): -2.6360, delta -0.0080, about 3.5 noise sd. It is a single run and has not been replicated, so it may be luck. Near misses, within noise of slot 9: slot 17 adaptive sd (-2.6354) and slot 28 walker (-2.6350). Weakly positive: slot 4 size-class start (-0.0024).

Did not help: SLSQP speed-ups and constraint forms (slots 0, 1, 2, 11), TIME_FRACTION 0.9, LP refit, staged jitter, remove-and-reinsert, short-iteration screening, alternative starts (sum r^p, Beta, lattice, pre-relaxation), swap and crossover moves, elite pools (+0.0092), always shaking (+0.0120), longer refinement maxiter, top-3 basin-hopping, and a 15% explore phase (-2.6318).

Next: 1) replicate slot 9 to confirm it. 2) Tune its perturbation size and restart fraction. 3) Combine it with the slot 4 start. 4) Skip micro-optimisations and further start-generation ideas.
